thread:
jonah: Heads up — FinCorp exec demo scheduled for Tue 10/14. They want a short POC showing streaming + schema-validated outputs + an example of orchestrating external tools (CRM lookup + secure vault). Also they asked about reserved capacity pricing and any enterprise blockers (SSO, IP allowlisting, KMS).

eva: On it. I can assemble a tiny app that streams tokens and emits a final JSON blob validated against a schema. Will need to confirm auth flow they prefer (service account vs short-lived creds).

mike: For vault/KMS integration we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments and KMS integration for Dedicated. For hosted POC we can demo envelope encryption and a mocked KMS. If they require HSM-backed keys that's an enterprise add-on.

sarah: Pricing note: if they want reserved capacity for predictable throughput we should quote monthly GPU commit + overage. For a 2-week POC we can use hosted credits and estimate cost by token/hour from their sample trace. I can draft a rough estimate if someone shares expected qps and avg seq len. :money_with_wings:

eva: Sample SDK snippet for streaming + schema output (python) — will attach to repo:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")

stream = client.generate_stream(model="rwd-large-1", prompt="Lookup customer and reply:")
for chunk in stream:
    print(chunk.text, end="")

# Final structured output (schema-validated)
final = client.generate(
    model="rwd-large-1",
    prompt="Produce JSON matching schema: {\"customer_id\":int, \"score\":float, \"action\":string}",
    output_schema={"type":"object","properties":{"customer_id":{"type":"integer"},"score":{"type":"number"},"action":{"type":"string"}},"required":["customer_id","action"]}
)
print(final.json)
```

jonah: Nice. Two integration questions from FinCorp: 1) can tool calls be proxied so their CRM never sees inbound traffic from our hosted infra? 2) Do we support schema enforcement on the runtime so we can auto-reject malformed outputs before invoking downstream systems?

eva: 1) Yes — we can demonstrate an adapter pattern: webhook -> customer proxy -> CRM, or a connector running in their VPC that calls the CRM. For demo we'll show a local proxy and explain on-prem connector. 2) Runtime can enforce schema at the model boundary (we run post-checks and can auto-fallback to a constrained prompt variant if validation fails). We'll include a small retry policy.

mike: On the proxy option: for hosted customers we recommend a short-lived credentials flow and a customer-side connector (lightweight) so the CRM never sees Redwood IPs. That avoids IP-allowlist friction. If they insist on static IPs we can offer NAT ranges for Dedicated/Private.

jonah: Enterprise blockers they mentioned: SSO (SAML), security questionnaire, and SOC2 evidence. Can sec-bot help triage which docs to send?

sec-bot: Sharing checklist: SSO flow (SAML 2.0 / OIDC), audit logs export (90 days default), KMS integration docs, SOC2 Type II summary, and network topology for Dedicated/Private. I can attach links in the thread.

sarah: For the quote: if they want rapid canary (small % traffic) on Reserved we should include one-off setup + an estimate for canary capacity. I can produce 3-tier options: hosted trial (credits), 3-month reserved pilot, 12-month committed.

eva: I'll spin up a minimal repo with two demos: (A) streaming UI that shows token-by-token and then the parsed JSON, (B) a small orchestrator that calls a CRM mock via a customer-side proxy. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

jonah: Perfect. Action items: eva attach repo + README with how to run proxy; mike prepare KMS/HSM note & IP range options; sarah draft three pricing tiers and a short note on POC credit usage; sec-bot attach security artifacts. I'll loop in the customer and propose times. :rocket:
